newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Up to 130,000/T of unclaimed oil product off China.
newsitem.headline: Up to 130,000/T of unclaimed oil product off China.

text.p: At least three fuel oil and gas oil cargoes totalling around 130,000 tonnes remained unclaimed off southern China with one cargo seen returning to Singapore, industry sources said on Monday.
"There is one 30,000-tonne cargo of gas oil which was scheduled for delivery (during) end-January which is already on its way back here," said a trader.
The cargoes have already been sold to Chinese endusers who have reneged on the deals. Sources said the seller is an oil trading firm based in Singapore.
"The cargo has been turned away by an enduser in China as it arrived two weeks late from the original date of arrival," the trader said.
Traders said three more gas oil and fuel oil cargoes that have also arrived off China late in January were "still on the table" with both buyers and sellers hammering out the terms to discharge them.
Sources said buyers in China, who had purchased oil products at very high prices in December, are reneging on the deals and cited "late deliveries" as the reason for not accepting the cargoes.
Gas oil prices have nosedived to the current $25.30-$25.70 per barrel from their peak of $34.45 on a free-on board (fob) basis in early December.
Fuel oil prices have also tumbled to around $99 a tonne from a peak of $124 a tonne, fob, in December.
Sources said these deals were done on an "open credit" basis and the sellers had not obtained any letters of credit.
A trader said the distressed fuel oil cargoes would probably fetch a maximum of about $102 a tonne on a cost and freight basis to southern China, down from $112-$113 a month ago.
